analysis:
This PR touches only the CI threat-review workflow and its documentation. It changes no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or cache code, so none of the canonical assets, boundaries or threats (A-001..A-017, TB-002, TB-011, T-0xx) are directly affected.

Workflow changes in .github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml:
- Removed the paid manual dispatch path: the pr_number input (base 9-12) and the API-resolved PR step (base 90-115).
- workflow_dispatch now defaults to the unpaid preflight (head 12).
- The review job runs only on non-draft pull_request_target events (head 68-69).
- Bedrock enablement no longer has the workflow_dispatch bypass. Forks still need BEDROCK_SCAN_ALLOW_FORKS (head 64). This narrows attack surface rather than widening it.
- Concurrency is keyed only by PR number (head 73).
- The job timeout rose from 20 to 60 minutes (head 55), with a 3000-second scanner deadline (head 131).
- The Bedrock call cap changed from the var-configurable BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_CALLS (default 12, base 162) to a hardcoded workload policy with BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS=100 (head 135-136).
- The scanner is still checked out from the default branch with persist-credentials false (head 77-83), so PR code is not executed.
- Clearance gating is unchanged (head 168-174).

The higher Bedrock ceiling is a CI billing consideration, not a provider-threat-model regression. Same-repo PRs require write access, and forks use Bedrock only when maintainers opt in. I recorded this as a cost and availability note for maintainers, not a finding.

Unverified contracts, in scripts not supplied:
- That the 'workload' call policy enforces the 100-call emergency ceiling.
- That GitHub job reruns perform no paid work.
- That incomplete reviews deny clearance, as claimed in changelog.d (lines 8-9) and docs/developer/test.md (729-735).

These live in .github/scripts and should be checked if those files change. The docs edits (build.md 258-261, test.md 729-735, changelog) are descriptive only.
